title: On-demand CSV delta exports with tenant-level envelope encryption and redaction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an on-demand customer usage export pathway that emits compact CSV deltas (changed rows only) with tenant-level envelope encryption and configurable redaction policies. This addresses large-tenant bandwidth/cost issues for nightly full CSVs and improves compliance by allowing per-tenant KMS-backed keys and deterministic redaction before storage or delivery. The export should support both S3 presigned fallback and webhook push, provide an ephemeral preview for customers in the Console, and retain deterministic row lineage metadata for resumption and reconciliations.
acceptance_criteria: API: Console can trigger an on-demand delta export (CSV) for a tenant + date range that returns a manifest with 1..n parts and lineage tokens
Security: Each export part is wrapped with tenant envelope encryption; keys can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed via KMS
Redaction: PII redaction rules (column-level) are applied deterministically and documented; sample rows in preview are masked and cannot be reversed by site staff
Delta correctness: Export only contains rows changed since last successful snapshot for the tenant and is idempotent when replayed
Delivery: Export parts are deliverable via S3 presigned URLs and webhook POST with retry/fanout semantics; both paths validate manifest checksums
Resume/Retry: Large exports can resume from part N using lineage tokens; resumable uploads honor SLA windows and backoff
Observability: Dashboard shows export latency, bytes/sec, part failures, retries, and per-tenant cost estimate before generate
Monitoring: Alerts exist for >5% part checksum failures across exports in a 1h window
tasks: Design data model for compact delta ledger (row GUID + op type + sequence) and lineage tokens
Prototype envelope encryption -> integrate with KMS shim (support AWS KMS + GCP KMS) and key rotation flows
Implement server-side deterministic redaction engine with pluggable policies and sample masking for previews
Extend export manifest schema to include part checksums, encryption metadata, lineage token, and redaction version
Add S3 presigned multipart upload generator and webhook fanout path with per-tenant backoff queues
Console UX: preview modal that streams first 100 masked rows and shows estimated size + cost impact
E2E tests: delta correctness across churn scenarios and resume tests with injected failures
Instrument metrics and add dashboards and alerts (Grafana + CloudWatch)
decision_log: Use envelope encryption with tenant DEK wrapped by KMS-managed KEK: balances performance and security; avoids full customer-side decryption in backend
Deterministic redaction chosen over tokenization to keep exports idempotent and resumable without maintaining a global pseudonym map
Delta approach: maintain per-tenant sequence checkpoint rather than per-row tombstone GC to keep export manifests small and allow fast diffs
Webhook vs S3: both supported. Primary delivery is webhook for low-latency customers; S3 presigned used as durable fallback for large exports or locked-down networks
Preview implementation will stream masked CSV rows from a short-lived staging copy (never exposing raw DEK) and revoke preview tokens after 5 minutes
tech_notes: Encryption: store envelope metadata in manifest: {alg:AES-GCM-256, dek-kms-key-id, dek-encrypted-blob, dek-version}
Redaction: implement policy DSL (column: method) where method in [mask, hash-sha256, redact-keep-last4, nullify]; record policy_version in manifest
Delta ledger: append-only per-tenant change stream persisted to partitioned Parquet; export service reads snapshot of change stream bounded by checkpoint
Performance: batch encryption per-part (8MB chunks) to amortize KMS usage and minimize API calls
DR: keep last 90 days of lineage checkpoints and manifests to allow customer reconciliation; older exports gated by support
